candidates.evidence: NASA states that Earth rotates once relative to the stars in 23 hours, 56 minutes, 4.09053 seconds; rounded to whole minutes gives 86,160 seconds.
candidates.familiarity: Earth’s rotation and the difference between a day and a full spin are common school astronomy topics, so many players can make a plausible estimate.

candidates.evidence: The USGS event page describes the 1964 magnitude 9.2 Alaska earthquake as lasting approximately 4.5 minutes, which equals 270 seconds.
candidates.familiarity: Major earthquakes and the 1964 Alaska quake appear in U.S. history, geography, and natural-disaster lessons, making the scale guessable.

candidates.evidence: The Beatles’ official song page lists the single’s length as 7:11, which converts to 431 seconds.
candidates.familiarity: “Hey Jude” is one of the Beatles’ best-known songs and is famous for its long singalong ending, so casual players may have a rough sense of its length.

candidates.evidence: Queen’s official News of the World track listing gives “We Will Rock You” as 2:01, which is 121 seconds.
candidates.familiarity: The stomp-stomp-clap anthem is widely heard at sports events, ads, and singalongs, and its short punchy form makes a rough estimate plausible.

candidates.evidence: Disney’s official page lists The Incredibles runtime as 1h 55min, which equals 6,900 seconds.
candidates.familiarity: This Pixar superhero film is a widely seen family movie, and feature-film lengths are familiar estimation territory for casual players.

candidates.evidence: Disney’s official page lists Sleeping Beauty runtime as 1h 14min, which equals 4,440 seconds.
candidates.familiarity: Sleeping Beauty is a classic Disney title many people encountered as children, and animated-movie runtimes are easy to roughly compare.

candidates.evidence: The NHL’s 2025–26 rulebook says intermissions are eighteen minutes long unless otherwise notified, equal to 1,080 seconds.
candidates.familiarity: Hockey intermissions are part of watching NHL games on TV or in arenas, so fans can make a reasonable estimate even if they do not know the rule exactly.
